query: How does resolution time vary across issue themes, channel, and priority?

per_column.name: issue_theme
per_column.rationale: Directly supplies the 'issue themes' axis the query names. Categorisations across all samples (billing, auth, outage, feature request, bug) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: operational_severity
per_column.rationale: A distinct severity axis useful for comparing resolution time; somewhat correlated with priority but adds finer granularity. Values (service_down for a full 502, minor for invoice) are well grounded in text.

per_column.name: blast_radius
per_column.rationale: Scope-of-impact gives a genuine new grouping axis. 'entire_tenant' for the Acme-wide outage and 'single_user' for the invoice are correct extractions; feature request as no_user_impact is reasonable.

per_column.name: root_cause_category
per_column.rationale: Useful modeling axis, and NULL/Unknown for silent rows is correct. However some values are confident inferences the text only weakly supports: the invoice duplicate labelled 'data_integrity' and the SSO session-drop labelled 'configuration_error' assert a cause the customer merely suspects, so some over-specification is present.

per_column.name: requires_escalation
per_column.rationale: Escalation path is a plausible operational axis. But values are largely inferred; e.g. the routine SSO/session case tagged 'engineering_escalation' is a judgement the text does not clearly establish, giving mild over-assertion.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Reasonable analytical dimension. Grounding is mostly sound (customer_has_workaround for the sed step, not_present for feature request), though 'no_workaround' vs 'not_present' distinction is somewhat inconsistently applied.

per_column.name: data_sensitivity_flag
per_column.rationale: A compliance/risk flag adds some leverage. Values are grounded (billing_financial_risk for invoice, not_present otherwise), but relevance to a resolution-time query is secondary.

per_column.name: data_sensitivity_or_compliance_flag
per_column.rationale: Near-duplicate of data_sensitivity_flag with essentially identical distribution and identical per-row values in every sample; it is a mere restatement adding no analytical leverage.

judge.rationale: Most added columns supply genuine, query-relevant axes (theme, severity, blast radius, root cause, escalation) that let the analyst slice resolution time in new ways, complementing the existing priority/channel fields. Grounding is generally sound with correct 'unknown'/'not_present' handling, though a few inference-heavy columns (root_cause_category, requires_escalation) over-assert causes the text only hints at. The one clear weakness is the pair of near-identical data_sensitivity columns, the second of which is a redundant restatement.
